• **Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**

 
 
• This **Ministry** was created as an independent entity on **15th October 1999** following the merger of the **Department of Statistics** and the **Department of Programme Implementation**.
 
• The **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under this ministry is responsible for the conduct of large-scale sample surveys and the **compilation of national accounts**, including the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
 
 
• **System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA):**
 
 
• The **SEEA framework** integrates economic and environmental data to provide a **multipurpose information system** for understanding the interactions between the **economy and the environment**.
 
• It facilitates the calculation of **Green GDP**, which adjusts the traditional **GDP** by accounting for **environmental degradation** and **resource depletion**.

• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the **nodal agency** for the planning, promotion, and coordination of **India's environmental and forestry programs**; however, the statistical compilation for **EnviStats** is handled by **MoSPI**.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** is primarily responsible for **internal security**, **border management**, and the **Census of India** (via the Registrar General).
 
• The **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** focuses on the **welfare and empowerment** of marginalized sections of society, such as **Scheduled Castes**, **OBCs**, and **persons with disabilities**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of EnviStats:**
 
 
• The report includes detailed accounts of **land cover**, **water use**, and **solid waste management** across different **Indian states and Union Territories**.
 
• By providing **time-series data**, it allows researchers to track **long-term environmental trends** and the efficiency of **government conservation schemes** like **Namami Gange** or the **National Afforestation Programme**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Context:** India is one of the few countries that have actively implemented the **SEEA framework** to produce **Environmental Accounts**, aligning its domestic statistical practices with **global benchmarks** set by the **United Nations**.
 
• **Data Sources:** The **MoSPI** collaborates with several technical agencies like the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, and **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)** to collect primary data for these statistical volumes.
 
• **Scope:** **EnviStats India** is typically released in **two volumes**: Volume I focuses on **Environmental Statistics** (based on the **FDES 2013** framework), while Volume II focuses on **Environmental Accounts**.

options.text: These are different from mental health and should be considered individually.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the passage's attitude toward these needs, we look at the final sentence: *"...care as the task of addressing adverse life circumstances... **while at the same time addressing needs related to security, relationship, daily accomplishment, or problem-solving**, is a very complicated story."*
 
• The use of the phrase **"while at the same time"** indicates that these practical and social needs (security, relationships, accomplishment) are not separate from mental health care but are **interconnected** with it.
 
• The "radical vision" described doesn't choose between fixing life circumstances and fixing the mind; it advocates for addressing **both** simultaneously.
 
• **Option 4** perfectly reflects this holistic attitude by stating these needs must be addressed **alongside** emotional and existential suffering.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The passage suggests they should be addressed "at the same time," which is the opposite of considering them "individually" or as "different from mental health."
 
• **Option 2:** This is **too restrictive**. The passage also mentions relationships, daily accomplishment, and problem-solving, not just security.
 
• **Option 3:** This **contradicts** the text, which explicitly includes these needs as part of the "task of care" in its complicated story.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level Reading Comprehension, look for "Integrative" keywords like "while," "simultaneously," or "at the same time." These words signal that the author views various elements as a **unified whole** rather than isolated parts.*

• **Equity:** Ensuring everyone has the specific tools they need to be successful, which is different from "equality" (giving everyone the same thing).
